profile.headline: Software Engineer and Coffee Shop Nostalgist

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
At Truss, I began to build my experience as a technical anchor and individual contributor. 

- Designed and implemented complex refactors that reduced technical debt and improved maintainability for a large legacy Go codebase
- Architected a Locust application w/ a complex API parser and customizable fake data generation that is used for robust load (>1000 concurrent users) and acceptance testing
- Spearheaded efforts to improve and consolidate documentation across sources into one Docusaurus site
- Established best practices for REST API design on a company level
- Founded and facilitated a learning/mentorship group for peers and juniors, presenting workshops on Docker, database design, CircleCI integrations, pointers, and more
- Greenfielded an experimental Django + GraphQL server, complete with process/workflow automation and query optimization to circumvent the n+1 problem

company.name: The University of Texas at Austin

positions.title: Senior Software Developer/Analyst
positions.description: After demonstrating my ability to succeed as a programmer, systems designer, technical lead, project lead, mentor, and instructor, I was promoted to the senior software developer role. In this role, I have completed software integrations with vendor products, led high-level strategic discussions about the technical progression of our team, and I have begun delving into new areas of development, such as building APIs and predictive modeling.

positions.title: Software Developer/Analyst
positions.description:
Software Developer/Analyst is the generic developer position at UT Austin. In this role, I continued my work on a large project to create an online application for the Hazlewood tuition exemption (available to Texas veterans and their relatives - tell your friends!). This involved designing the database schema from scratch using Oracle, and building out the Python/Django code base to go with it. 

Our student-facing front-end had one peculiar requirement: It had to be completely functional without JavaScript, while also being mobile-friendly. While my colleague designed the staff side of the portal, I took on this challenge with the student side. In the end, it was beautifully functional with JavaScript/JQuery/Bootstrap, and fully accessible without. It was extremely well-received throughout campus, and revolutionized the student experience of applying for this tuition exemption. It also greatly reduced the time staff spent processing these applications - turn around for decisions went from 15 or more business days to 5-8 days max. 

Thanks to the massive success of this project, I became the lead of another large-scale project, similarly involving database design all the way to the front-end. To deliver this on a tight deadline, I coordinated a group of 5 developers, keeping us all on track to meet our goals, and ultimately delivered another successful product. At the end of the development cycle, I worked closely with my clients and users to lead training sessions and write robust documentation for this new system. I gained a positive reputation for being clear, concise, and above all, incredibly helpful and generous with my time. Of course, my clients were completely wonderful and deserve much of the credit for this :) 

Meanwhile, I joined a group of developers leading the push to implement more modern tools in our tech stack, and I became an active contributor to campus-wide training efforts that have been bringing new, promising developers into UT.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
After completing training, I spent another six months in the role of Software Developer, the junior  developer role at UT. I spent my time learning the ins-and-outs of reporting and batch processes (cron jobs), computing stats for system analysis using SAS, fixing bugs and performing maintenance on massive systems (Course Scheduling), and eventually joining a large project as the second technical lead.

I soaked up all the knowledge thrown at me during this time, and grew an enormous amount. My supervisor saw this, and I was promoted to the next level of developer sooner than what was seen in many other departments (1 year).

positions.title: Software Developer Trainee
positions.description: For a short time period, UT (the Office of the Registrar, to be specific) trained me in their tech stack: Natural/ADABAS for use with the mainframe, and Python/Django for web development. This ran like a boot camp or online course, but it was full-time, paid, and onsite. I needed to demonstrate time management, self-motivated learning, the ability to ask meaningful questions but also research answers on my own, and effective project structure and management. Throughout the training, my performance was evaluated by my supervisors and future peers, and I "graduated" with excellent feedback.

positions.title: Pharmacy Clerk
positions.description:
As a pharmacy clerk, I logged inventories, stocked shelves, served customers efficiently and pleasantly, and maintained the pharmacy computer systems to provide the most accurate and informed service possible. It was also my job to interact with medical professionals and insurance representatives, both through faxes and on the phone, to resolve issues with customers' prescriptions and find ways to overcome payment barriers. 

This job highlighted the complexities and struggles within our current health care system, many of which I hadn't been exposed to previously. In particular, the nuance of the cash price of medication sometimes being cheaper than the copay with insurance surprised me - I learned to triple-check pricing and read over our clients' plans to make sure we were always charging them the lowest amounts possible.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
The SHAVE (Severe Hazards Analysis & Verification) project researched hail and flood data by gathering individual accounts of storm activity and comparing those details with actual radar output. My job involved monitoring radar feedback from across the contiguous United States, analyzing that information to identify the weather patterns relevant to our study, and then fluidly shifting our priorities based on when and where important storms were developing.

My team had to work within tight time constraints (interviews conducted more than 30 minutes after the storm had passed were inadmissible due to the fickleness of memory) to obtain reliable data by calling residents and surveying them about their experiences. This work involved a delicate balance of picking houses in the best locations for an ideal data swath, building trust and an affable rapport during phone calls to encourage detailed responses, and bouncing back from any set-backs.

positions.title: Office Intern
positions.description: OK ABLE Tech is an organization that aims to connect disabled and disadvantaged Oklahomans with the medical equipment they need. While working here, I maintained the online inventory system and reorganized physical inventory spaces to be more intuitive. I also created charts, fact sheets, and maps using Excel and GIMP.

honors.title: 2019 Cathy Lester IT Rising Star Award
honors.description:
The Cathy Lester IT Rising Star Award is a distinction that The University of Texas developer community grants to "someone early in their IT career who shows extraordinary promise" (from https://sites.utexas.edu/cll/about-the-award/).  

I was honored to receive this award after two rewarding years working as a software developer for UT. From my official nomination:

"She has lead major projects; she’s made valuable contributions as a team member; she’s learned difficult business areas inside-out; she’s forged excellent relationships with business users; she’s been an education coordinator for our in-house SD training program; and she’s accomplished all this superhuman activity without showing a whiff of stress."
honors.issuer: Issued by Cathy Lester IT Excellence Committee · Apr 2019
